Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve a smaller piece of a larger problem. Every recursive function needs a base case, which is a simple condition that tells the function to stop calling itself. Without this stopping point, the program would get trapped in an infinite loop and eventually crash. You can think of it like Russian nesting dolls, where you keep opening each smaller doll until you finally reach the solid one at the very center.
